Description

Bradykinin formed in the inflamed OA joint binds the B2 receptor on nociceptor endings. The receptor activates the G protein Gq, whose α subunit stimulates phospholipase Cβ, and RGS proteins end the signal by accelerating GTP hydrolysis. Blocking the B2 receptor inside the joint reduces pain in rats with iodoacetate-induced OA and has been reported to relieve pain in knee OA.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, GTP and GDP included, as it works for the block's result. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: bradykinin excites and sensitises nociceptors.
